title: Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
main_claim: For d>=3 and every spin S, there is beta_0(d,S) such that for every beta>=beta_0 the nearest-neighbour isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet has a translation-invariant beta-KMS state for the zero-field dynamics with omega(S_0^z)>=S/4.
coverage: I read all eight sections of the LaTeX (about 3.9k lines) and checked each step of the main chain. (1) §1 slot/loop representation: rates, the e^{beta q/4} normalisation, the spectral law, the factorial/Mecke domination via the 2^n insertion ratio. (2) §2 pin test: stability of the layered permutation symbol under partial symmetrisation, the splicing that extracts a coefficient of t (cycles missing P give a factor 2), negative dependence of sigma(T) giving the bound r^m, the comparison w_P<=w_E<=2^m w_P, and the dense-boundary limit. (3) §3 exposure disintegration (two-clock construction, branch identity 2^{n_P}=sum_A 1_{F_A}2^{c_A}1_{G_P}), the exterior-moment identity for Bernoulli transpositions, and Prop 3.3. I verified Prop 3.3 numerically in python on a random product of Bernoulli transpositions and fixed permutations (n=5, |J|=2): P(G_J)=det(I-K_QQ) and E[Sigma|G_J]=K_JJ+K_JQ(I-K_QQ)^{-1}K_QJ match exactly. Also the return-energy identity <f,(I-U)f>=sum_T(1-(U*f)_i). (4) §4: blocking at non-grid times via the factorial bound, binary-witness sparsity and counting (b^alpha>4, separation h_j/4), the regularity probability, local connectivity, and the Nash transfer. (5) §5: hull laminarity and clearance, plaquette connectivity of the boundary, the orthant flow divergence, congestion C(1+h)^{d nu}, overlap exponent 2k-d>alpha, energy C m R^alpha. (6) §6: the exact loss identity, the two-ends Cauchy–Schwarz bound, the localization count (2Ks)^R/R!, the Nash ODE under regular time plus Markov's inequality, discarded-pairing bounds, weighted Young (int w^2/W = 4/s), and the exponents 1.089, 1.639, 2.689 > 1, so eps(p)=o(p). (7) §7: the surface-cost bound via Jensen, conditional mean spin (1/2)(1-P(i in B)), the field tail with h_N=N^{-1/2}, the rotation formula, the trace-cyclicity top edge, and the strip-limit lemma. I did not independently re-derive the cited external results (BBL Thm 4.20/4.9, Nachtergaele–Ogata–Sims existence). Their use here is either reproved in the text or only used for standard facts.

issues.description: The bound by subsets uses that at least ceil(n/2) sites were blocked at the preceding grid time q, applied through I_p(P) to the chosen slots at time q. This implicitly needs those chosen slot points not to lie in P at time q, which the text handles only for the full-set case ('If any chosen slot is pinned... blocking is impossible'). The same remark applies verbatim to subsets, so the step is correct, but it is stated tersely.
issues.evidence: 'summing (4.5) over subsets costs at most 2^n p^{ceil(n/2)}'; (4.5) is derived only for prescribed sparse sets via one fixed slot per site.

sibling_notes: No sibling entries were in family 271 when I checked. The determinant-preserving next-pin identity (Prop 3.3) is the key novel tool. It checks out exactly in a numerical test, so companion papers using it can rely on it.
